Cohort 1 is 25 named venues in the CRM, each carrying a verified buyer contact with a verification date within 30 days of the send, a verified email address, coordinates that plot inside the 45-minute drive-time ring, eligibility confirmed against D-012's in and out venue-type lists, and one written venue-specific reason it belongs. Evidence: the CRM completeness export by field, held in Signal HQ and never in the project tree. Any blank verification date means the cohort is not locked. (E10.06, E10.07, E10.08, E10.11, E10.12, R-005)

The researched universe is at least 125 accounts, or the shortfall is formally documented with the number actually found and what was searched. Deduplication is complete across venue groups, multi-property hotels, shared operators and renamed properties, with the number of merged rows recorded. Evidence: the universe count and the dedup log. This is the criterion that says out loud whether 25 signed venues is arithmetically available. (E10.04, E10.05)

Deliverability is proven before the first real send, not assumed. SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass on signalstudio.ie as shown by raw headers on a real received message rather than by a DNS record existing; the domain's sending history is stated; and an inbox-placement test to a seed set across Gmail, Outlook and one Irish ISP records where each message landed. Evidence: the raw headers, the seed results, the dates. (E11.04, R-010)

Sending mechanics match D-013 exactly and are verifiable from the sent message rather than the configuration screen: film link-click tracking on, open tracking off with no tracking pixel present in the HTML, a one-click unsubscribe header, and a suppression list honoured by the sending path. Evidence: the raw source of a real test send showing no pixel and the unsubscribe header, plus a test that a suppressed address is refused. (D-013 point 3, E11.04, E03.11)

The complete sequence has been rehearsed once, end to end, against a rehearsal account before any real venue is touched: introduction email sent and received, film link clicked, meeting booked through the booking flow, discovery structure used, walkthrough delivered, proposal and order form issued, 14-day hold started, and the account moved through every CRM stage including 'later' after the fourth touch. Evidence: the rehearsal account's full stage history, the artifacts produced at each step, and a written list of what broke. A sequence never walked is a document, not a system. (E11.02, E11.05, E11.08 to E11.11, E11.13, E11.14, D-013 point 4)

The venue marketing-controls package exists and is attached to the agreement, not only to the pack: the approved copy pack, a one-page prohibited-claims sheet naming 'forever', 'guaranteed', permanence or storage promises, 'GDPR compliant' and any claim that legal review was obtained, and the clause in the master agreement requiring correction within a stated period. Evidence: the copy pack, the sheet, and the clause reference in the E03.02 draft. R-020 is the only risk on the register that reaches outside Signal Studio's own strings. (R-020, E03.02, E12.12)

Every commercial surface a Cohort 1 venue can reach is enumerated as a list and QA'd per dimension: the public landing page, the private Founding 25 invitation page, the parameterised proposal page, the film landing destination, the certificate, the sales kit, the deck and the one-page proposal. Each has a recorded verdict on copy, price presentation, privacy explanation, responsive, accessibility and performance. Evidence: the surface list with a verdict per dimension per surface. A surface not on the list is a surface nobody checked. (E12.01 to E12.14)

The price is presented identically wherever a venue can see it: EUR 1,500 standard, EUR 1,000 founding, both inclusive of VAT at the prevailing rate, annual prepaid, with the founding conditions attached, including the schema.org offer markup in studio/src/app/layout.tsx. Evidence: a per-surface string sweep confirming no surface states a price without the VAT wording and the conditions. (E12.04, D-009, D-021)

The personalised delivery path works end to end for one venue before it runs for 25: a tracked link is generated, resolves to that venue's landing destination, plays the film without a large attachment, records the click, and the click appears in the founder operating dashboard. Evidence: the test link, the recorded click, the dashboard row. (E11.07, E13.16, E09.04, E09.05)

The objection library answers the questions this specific offer creates, with a written answer per question matching the ratified position rather than improvising a new one: why EUR 1,000 and not EUR 1,500; what the price lock does on a venue sale; what unlimited means and what happens at fair use; what the venue sees and never sees; whether a solicitor reviewed the contract, using the pre-approved answer from the legal gate; what happens to couples if Signal Studio stops; and why there is no in-person meeting. Evidence: the library plus a cross-check of each answer against its D-number. (E11.12, E12.08, D-016, D-018)

Consent is tracked per venue before any name is published. The E10.14 consent field is populated for every Cohort 1 account, and the map, the site and the certificate publish only where consent is recorded. Evidence: the consent field state per account and a check that the published surfaces name only consented venues. (E10.14, E15.16, PROJECT.md section 21)

No contact data has leaked into the project tree or a generated report. project-control.mjs validate passes, private/venues.csv is confirmed gitignored and untracked via git ls-files, and a scan of PROJECT_STATE.json, STATUS.md, BACKLOG.md and evidence/ finds no email address, phone number, postal address or venue name presented as a participant. Evidence: the scan output and the git ls-files result. (PROJECT.md section 21, REPORTING.md section 5)
